featureFlags.rwb.p3.refdata-versions: this story; default false, true in the local profile; bound by the package-private RefdataSettings record (prefix rwb.p3). The read beans (ReferenceDataService, ReferenceDataReaders) and ReferenceTableHandlers exist whatever the flag; ReferenceDataReaders.enabled() returns it; the registry's recordVersion, approve and rollback refuse when it is off; the controller and dispatcher are mapped when this flag OR rwb.p3.configservice is on.
featureFlags.mapping: @ConditionalOnExpression("${rwb.p3.refdata-versions:false} or ${rwb.p3.configservice:false}") on ReferenceLoadController and ReferenceLoadDispatcher only. A request routed to a branch whose flag is off gets 404 MSG-P4-003 (not in API v4, GAP-48); both off means no mapping (404 from the security filter). No RecoveryFlags or RecoveryProperties change.

loadCheckOrder: L1 authenticated; ActorIdResolver resolves oid or sub as a UUID; else 401 MSG-P4-001 (ApiError.NO_ROLE)
L2 area right Reference data C through CapabilityCheck.require; else 403 MSG-P4-002 with action 'load reference data' and one REFUSED audit
L3 table present and not blank; the authority grants the table right when it is absent so the controller answers 422 MSG-GEN-001 field=table, with no REFUSED audit (finding 136; TC-FD-01)

L4a code known: a registered handler, or a catalog row rwb.refload.loader.<code>; an unknown code passes the table right and is refused 422 later (SPEC-002; this keeps TC-BR1's rule/HOLIDAY 422 and SEC-06's 403 both true)
L4 table right: the caller's role intersects rwb.refload.loader.<code>; missing or empty refuses 403 MSG-P4-002 and one REFUSED audit
L5 registry branch flag on; else 404 MSG-P4-003
L6 file and validFrom present and parseable; else 422 MSG-GEN-001 field
L7 file readable (CSV or XLSX); else 422 MSG-P3-027 check 'the file cannot be read'
L8 at least one data row; else 422 MSG-GEN-001 rows

L9 early repeat only for a handler code whose repeatMessage(file) is present: the same (table, validFrom, content_hash) exists gives 409 with that message, nothing written, for any business date (findings 133, 140; A-38; GAP-56)
L10 validFrom at or after the business date; else 422 MSG-P3-027 check 'valid from is before the business date'

L11 every other code, in the story order: the same (table, validFrom, content_hash) gives 201 with the existing body, nothing written (A-06); else an APPROVED twin with this validFrom gives 409 MSG-P3-027

L12 the table code check for a built-in (active LOV code and a definition that is not none; else 422 'table code is not a reference table' or 'no column definition for the table'), then the column definition and row check when a definition exists; a handler code skips the LOV/definition requirement but runs the definition check when one exists
L13 handler.validate; 422 with the first failure's messageCode, placeholders and field, and detail listing every failure in order, capped at 100 with the total
L14 row_key unique in the file; else 422 MSG-P3-027 check 'row key repeated'
L15 record the VALIDATED version in one transaction; audit DONE with changeSummary after commit
handlerContract.messagePassThrough: handler message IDs and ApiProblemException pass through unchanged; MSG-P3-027 is used only for the registry's own checks; any other exception in validate is a defect (500, nothing written), in apply or onRolledBack the transaction rolls back and the answer is 409 MSG-GEN-004
handlerContract.rowKey: keyColumns() joined by a vertical bar; else the definition's K columns; else the 6-digit data row number (A-37); unique per version, max 200 characters
owningStorySupplies: the handler bean of type access.api.ReferenceTableHandler behind its own flag, depending on P4 only, declaring dating() (CURRENT_STATE unless its table holds dated versions; A-42)
the two parameter_catalog rows rwb.refload.loader.<code> and rwb.refload.approver.<code> (CODE_LIST, BUSINESS, GLOBAL, required=false, owner RW-RISK) in the catalog file and its own migration
its message IDs in RWB-E1-042's message catalog
handlerContract.dataProduct: RWB-E1-001: P4 SPI implementation, imports nothing from casewf; keyColumns product_code; dating CURRENT_STATE (PS6 uk_data_product; GAP-54); its K0-K5 messages pass through; repeatMessage MSG-P1-011 (409, early repeat L9); no refdata.columns.data_product; loader RW-REFADM, approver RW-DATASTEW (A-40; GAP-46); no LOV-REF-TABLE change; approved and applied on validFrom, writing data_product.valid_from (S7-001 flow step 10)
handlerContract.effectiveDate: DATED: apply (at approval) stores the version dated by validFrom and never changes what a reader gets for an earlier business date; versions are independent; onRolledBack follows the same rule. CURRENT_STATE (default; data_product, sys_fields): approval refused 409 MSG-P3-027 while validFrom is after the business date; apply runs at once when validFrom is at or before the business date (with A-17, on the valid-from date); rollback re-applies the restored version at once; no owner job and no schema change (SPEC-025, SPEC-032 rules 5-6; A-42; finding 138). At most one APPROVED version per validFrom for every code, so a same-day correction of a CURRENT_STATE table needs a rollback first (which needs an earlier approved version, else 409 MSG-P3-015) or waits for a later validFrom (findings 147, 154).

problemBody: application/problem+json: type, title, status, detail, messageCode, messageTh, field, traceId (API Specification v4 Problem). The 403 uses MSG-P4-002 with {action} 'load reference data', 'approve reference data' or 'roll back reference data', never 'do this' (A-45; finding 142). The 500 is the existing ApiExceptionHandler.unexpected body and carries no traceId (PG-E1-043-03); ReferenceLoadIT#rowKeyAndHandlerDefect asserts that body and the absence of traceId, and the field is requested separately (R18).
